n: Two years later (December 518 BC), a new message comes. The temple was about halfway finished.
People from Bethel send a delegation to seek the Lord at the temple.

f.g: Leaders of the delegation; their Babylonian-style names show exile’s influence.

n: Their question: “Should we keep mourning and fasting in the fifth month, as we have for so many years?” They had fasted yearly to remember the temple’s destruction. Now that it was being rebuilt, was it still needed?
The Lord answers through Zechariah — but not right away with a yes or no.

f.w: the word of the LORD of hosts
f.g: God’s answer goes deeper than the question.

n: When you fasted all those seventy years, was it really for Me? God asks them to examine their motives.

f.g: The seventh-month fast recalled the murder of governor Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:25).

f.w: did ye at all fast unto me

n: And when you ate and drank at feasts, wasn’t that for yourselves too? Religious practices can become self-centered.

f.w: did not ye eat for yourselves

n: Isn’t this the same message the earlier prophets gave when Jerusalem was prosperous and the land was full of people? The answer was already given before the exile.

f.g: The Negev (southern desert) and the Shephelah (foothills).

n: Zechariah restates the earlier prophets’ core message.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto Zechariah
f.g: Introducing a summary of the prophets’ message.

n: Judge with true justice; show kindness and compassion to each other. This matters more to God than rituals.
Don’t oppress widows, orphans, foreigners, or the poor, and don’t even plot evil against one another in your hearts. God cares about the vulnerable.

f.w: oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless

n: But their ancestors refused to listen. Like a stubborn ox, they jerked their shoulder away and plugged their ears.

f.g: Like an ox refusing the yoke.

n: They made their hearts hard as flint to avoid hearing God’s law and the words His Spirit spoke through the prophets. So great anger came.

f.w: they made their hearts as an adamant stone

n: Because they wouldn’t listen when God called, God wouldn’t listen when they called.

f.w: they cried, and I would not hear

n: So God scattered them like a whirlwind among unknown nations, and the beautiful land became desolate. Their own choices ruined “the pleasant land.”

f.w: I scattered them with a whirlwind
